Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO. 78 DEC 04 OSCAR C. PERALTA Punong Barangay Barangay Luz & Kitang II Municipality of Limay Province of Bataan Dear PB Peralta: This has reference to your letter dated August 23, 2023 requesting this Department's legal opinion regarding your suspension as the Punong Barangay of Barangay Luz & Kitang II. Per the representation, you were suspended for the period of three (3) months as a penalty for Grave Misconduct and Gross Neglect of Duty. You then represented that on June 6, 2023, while serving the penalty of suspension, you were charged again by the two Sanggunian Barangay Members of Barangay Luz & Kitang II for two cases of Grave Misconduct for another offense. You stated that on July 31, 2023, the Sanggunian Bayan of Limay dismissed the two cases for Grave Misconduct but you were still given the penalty of suspension and was penalized for the offense of Conduct Unbecoming of a Public Official and was found guilty for violation of R.A. 8941, otherwise known as the "Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines. Thus, the request for legal opinion on the following: 1. 2. 3. Whether a Punong Barangay may still be charged and suspended for another offense even if they are currently serving the penalty of suspension for a previous offense; Whether the suspension as a penalty may be lifted during the 90-day election period; and Whether the Sanggunian Bayan of Limay erred in finding you as guilty of conduct unbecoming and for violation of R.A. 8941 As to the first query, we answer in the positive. Please be apprised that if new and distinct allegations of misconduct or violations of rules and regulations arise during the course of a public official's suspension, it is still possible to initiate a new disciplinary proceeding against that official. Also, the penalty for the subsequent offense is different from the previous offense as they are different causes of action, hence, different penalties. In case the public official "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

was found to be guilty of the subsequent offense, the subsequent penalty of suspension would be related to the new charge/s. As to the second query, this was already clarified by this Department in its legal opinion no. 51 s. 20231. The salient parts of which are as follows: "Let it be noted further that Section 2 (c) of the LGC governs only those preventive suspensions imposed by the sangguniang bayan, sanggguniang panglungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan and the Office of the President. It is inapplicable to the preventive suspension imposed by the Office of the Ombudsman and the Sandiganbayan which are guided by different laws, rules, and regulations as the Ombudsman Act and the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. As regards suspension as a penalty, Section 62 (c) of the LGC only mentioned about the prohibition on the imposition of preventive suspension and does not include suspension as a penalty. Hence, suspension as a penalty may still be imposed by the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan and the Office of the President notwithstanding the onset of the 90-day period. As to the difference of suspension as a preventive measure and suspension as a penalty, the case of Quimbo V. Gervaci02 is instructive, thus: "Preventive suspension is merely a preventive measure, a preliminary step in the administrative investigation. The purpose of the suspension is to prevent the accused from using his position and the powers and prerogative of his office to influence potential witnesses or tamper with records which may be vital inn the prosecution of the case against him. If after such investigation, the charge is established and the person investigated is found guilty of acts warranting his suspension or removal, then he is suspended, removed or dismissed. This is the penalty." Based on the foregoing, we clarify that starting August I, 2023 up to October 29, 2023 (90-day period contemplated under Section 62 (c) of the LGC) - the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan and the Office of the President can no longer impose preventive suspension upon local elective officials.3 If the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan and the Office of the President had imposed preventive suspension upon local elective officials prior to August I, 2023, and will last thereafter, such preventive suspension shall be deemed automatically lifted on August I, 2023.4 As to the üæLgugm_pIease be informed that this department is precluded from acting on queries and matters which are those containing facts that are justiciable nature. DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010 specifically provides: July 31, 2023 2 G.R. No. 155620, August 9, 2005 3 Supra at 1 4 Ibid Page 2 of 3

1. "xxx all concerned are hereby advised that the Department shall not an act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy; Xxxx" (emphasis supplied) From the foregoing, considering that the matter contains facts that are justiciable in nature, this department is devoid of authority to act on the matter. Thus, the Department has no jurisdiction to act on the query, and it is best addressed by the proper tribunal with proper jurisdiction. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, B UTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: T . JUA ICTOR R.
